```{r} #| label: setup #| message: false #| warning: false #| include: false library(tidyverse) library(scales) library(knitr) library(kableExtra) # fonts ---- library(extrafont) library(sysfonts) source("_common.R") # use font showtext::showtext_auto() # set theme ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_toysrus( base_size = 15)) # pak::pak("wilkox/treemapify") library(treemapify) ``` ```{r} #| label: status #| results: "asis" #| echo: false # status ---- # polish, dev, draft, complete status("complete") ``` :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}
```{r} #| label: full_code_display #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '60%' #| out-width: '60%' #| fig-align: right library(treemapify) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) set.seed(1999) toy_sales <- tibble( department = c("Electronic pets", "Electronic pets", "Plush", "Plush", "Video games", "Video games"), toy = c("Furby", "Tamagotchi", "Beanie Babies", "Tickle Me Elmo", "Game Boy Color", "Nintendo 64"), yearly_rate = c(1800, 900, 2400, 700, 1200, 1000), holiday_share = c(0.80, 0.40, 0.35, 0.60, 0.55, 0.50)) |> tidyr::expand_grid(season = c("Holiday", "Rest of year")) |> mutate(lambda = yearly_rate * if_else(season == "Holiday", holiday_share, 1 - holiday_share), units = rpois(n(), lambda = lambda)) |> select(department, toy, season, lambda, units) labs_treemap <- labs( title = "Toys\"R\"Us 1998", caption = "Simulated data", fill = "Season") ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(toy_sales, aes(area = units, fill = season, label = season, subgroup = department, subgroup2 = toy)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_text( place = "bottomright", color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, alpha = 0.90, fontface = "italic", family = "sans") ggp2_tm_subgroup <- ggp2_treemap + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border( color = "#0057B8", size = 4.0) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text( place = "center", alpha = 0.75, color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, family = "sans") ggp2_tm_subgroup2 <- ggp2_tm_subgroup + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border( color = "#FFD200", size = 4) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_text( place = "topleft", alpha = 0.65, grow = TRUE, color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, family = "mono", fontface = "bold") ggp2_tm_subgroup2 + labs_treemap ``` ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ at least two categorical variables** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric variable of counts (for each level of the categorical variables)** ::: :::: ## Description Treemaps display proportionally divided rectangular hierarchies for levels of categorical variables. The layout consists of 'squarified' tiles, which display the relative contribution of each categorical value to the overall graph space. We'll build a treemap using the [`treemapify` package.](http://wilkox.org/treemapify/) Also check out the [mosaic plots](mosaic_plots.qmd) chapter. ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Install packages. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: pkg_code_treemap #| code-fold: show #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| results: hide # pak::pak("wilkox/treemapify") library(treemapify) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation library(tidyr) # for expand_grid() ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: The 1998 holiday season at Toys"R"Us belonged to Furby, but Beanie Babies, Tamagotchis, and the Game Boy Color kept the aisles busy all year. We'll simulate one store's unit sales for six toys in three departments. Each toy gets a `yearly_rate` (the units we'd expect to sell in a year) and a `holiday_share` (the part of those sales that land in November and December). `tidyr::expand_grid()` creates a row for each toy in each `season`, `lambda` splits the yearly rate between the two seasons, and `rpois()` draws the units sold. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same sales every time you run the code below. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: data_code_treemap #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true set.seed(1999) toy_sales <- tibble( department = c("Electronic pets", "Electronic pets", "Plush", "Plush", "Video games", "Video games"), toy = c("Furby", "Tamagotchi", "Beanie Babies", "Tickle Me Elmo", "Game Boy Color", "Nintendo 64"), yearly_rate = c(1800, 900, 2400, 700, 1200, 1000), holiday_share = c(0.80, 0.40, 0.35, 0.60, 0.55, 0.50)) |> tidyr::expand_grid(season = c("Holiday", "Rest of year")) |> mutate(lambda = yearly_rate * if_else(season == "Holiday", holiday_share, 1 - holiday_share), units = rpois(n(), lambda = lambda)) |> select(department, toy, season, lambda, units) glimpse(toy_sales) ``` ::: ## Distribution A treemap nests counts inside counts: seasons inside toys, and toys inside departments. Every tile's area is a share of the store's total sales, so the question behind the graph is "how much of the whole does each piece take up?" Below we'll move from the sales, to a picture, to the formula. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with the rows for Furby and Beanie Babies. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: count_values_treemap #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true toy_sales |> filter(toy %in% c("Furby", "Beanie Babies")) ``` ::: Each simulated count (`units`) lands within a few percent of the rate we gave `rpois()` (`lambda`). Furby sold most of its units during the holidays, while Beanie Babies sold most of theirs during the rest of the year. Adding up the counts inside each department gives the department totals, and dividing by the store total turns them into the shares the treemap draws. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: count_summary_treemap #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true toy_sales |> group_by(department) |> summarise(units = sum(units), expected = sum(lambda)) |> mutate(share = round(units / sum(units), 3)) ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: A bar model shows the hierarchy one level at a time. Each department is a bar, each toy is a part of its department's bar, and each part is split by season. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: draw_bar_model_treemap #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true ggplot(toy_sales, aes(x = units, y = toy, fill = season)) + geom_col() + facet_grid(department ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") + labs(x = "Units sold", y = NULL, fill = "Season") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: A treemap takes the same parts and packs them into one rectangle. Below, the yellow borders outline the departments, the blue borders outline the toys, and the colors split each toy by season. The Furby tile is almost all holiday sales, and the Beanie Babies tile is mostly the rest of the year. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: draw_treemap #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true ggplot(toy_sales, aes(area = units, fill = season, subgroup = department, subgroup2 = toy)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(color = "#0057B8", size = 3) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text(color = "#FFFFFF", place = "center", min.size = 0, family = "sans") + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border(color = "#FFD200", size = 6) + labs(fill = "Season") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Each toy and season count comes from a [Poisson distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution): $$ N_{\text{toy, season}} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_{\text{toy, season}}) $$ Poisson counts have a useful property for treemaps: the sum of independent Poisson counts is also Poisson, with a rate equal to the sum of the rates. So each department total is $\text{Poisson}(\sum \lambda)$: 2,700 for electronic pets, 3,100 for plush, and 2,200 for video games. The standard deviation of a Poisson count is $\sqrt{\lambda}$, so its relative wobble is $\sqrt{\lambda} / \lambda = 1 / \sqrt{\lambda}$. For the Furby holiday tile ($\lambda = 1{,}440$) that's under 3%, which is why the treemap's tiles barely change shape from one simulation to the next. Try dividing every `yearly_rate` by 100 and the small tiles start to jump around. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: - Create labels with `labs()` - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` - Map the `units` to `area`, `season` to `fill` and `label`, `department` to `subgroup`, and `toy` to `subgroup2` - Add `geom_treemap()` - Add `geom_treemap_text()` - `place`: this controls where the boxes start - `color`: text color - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing) - `alpha`: opacity - `fontface`: `itlalic`/`bond` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: code_graph_treemap #| code-fold: show #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' labs_treemap <- labs( title = "Toys\"R\"Us 1998", caption = "Simulated data", fill = "Season") ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(toy_sales, aes(area = units, fill = season, label = season, subgroup = department, subgroup2 = toy)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_text( place = "bottomright", color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, alpha = 0.90, fontface = "italic", family = "sans") ggp2_treemap + labs_treemap ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: create_graph_treemap #| eval: true #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 labs_treemap <- labs( title = "Toys\"R\"Us 1998", caption = "Simulated data", fill = "Season") ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(toy_sales, aes(area = units, fill = season, label = season, subgroup = department, subgroup2 = toy)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_text( place = "bottomright", color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, alpha = 0.90, fontface = "italic", family = "sans") ggp2_treemap + labs_treemap ``` ::: ## More info `treemapify` has multiple options for building treemaps. We cover a few of these below, but you should check out the [package vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html). ### Subgroup `ggplot2` build layers in the order they're written, so it's [advised](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html) to build the subgroups in order from "*from deepest to shallowest*", with `subgroups2` first (ending on `subgroup`) - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup2_border()` - Set the `size` and `color` - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup2_text()` - `place`: this controls where the boxes start - `color`: text color - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing) - `alpha`: opacity - `fontface`: `itlalic`/`bond` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` See full list of arguments [here](http://wilkox.org/treemapify/). ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: code_graph_treemap_sgb #| eval: true #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 ggp2_tm_subgroup <- ggp2_treemap + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border( color = "#0057B8", size = 4.0) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text( place = "center", alpha = 0.75, color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, family = "sans") ggp2_tm_subgroup + labs_treemap ``` ::: ### Subgroup 2 - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup_border()` - Set the `size` and `color` - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup_text()` - `place`: this controls where the boxes start - `color`: text color - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing) - `alpha`: opacity - `fontface`: `itlalic`/`bond` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: code_graph_tmap_sgb_2 #| eval: true #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 ggp2_tm_subgroup2 <- ggp2_tm_subgroup + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border( color = "#FFD200", size = 4) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_text( place = "topleft", alpha = 0.65, grow = TRUE, color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, family = "mono", fontface = "bold") ggp2_tm_subgroup2 + labs_treemap ``` :::
